description: A large terrain cut into square tiles that join without seams. The map is a heightfield of about 256 cells a side: the cell is a power of two in metres (exact in binary, so a tile's samples sit exactly where the map's do) and the side is map_size rounded to whole tiles of whole cells, so tile borders fall on samples. Domain-warped perlin hills, absolute terraces (relief / 8 apart) turn their contours into winding escarpments, fine noise roughens them, and a river winding along X cuts its valley down to a floor that falls from +X to -X (layer water); a blur softens it all and a clip keeps the ground between 0 and relief. The tile (tile_x, tile_z, kept within the map) is cooked on its own: the same grid, cropped to the tile with a margin of 6 samples for the blur (heightfield_crop), run through the same nodes and cropped back to its core. Every step works at world positions, so the tile gets the samples of the map where it lies; assert seamless compares them, sample for sample, and assert height checks that the map stays between 0 and relief. Node showcase (not an output) draws the map with a dark frame on the tile's spot and the tile lifted above it on lines from its corners, coloured by absolute height.
